question: What host-authorized boundary should govern Claw-provided stdio commands and reuse of globally named MCP declarations?
rationale: The patch establishes a durable ownership model, but whether Claws may introduce executable commands or share a global MCP resource is a security and product policy decision that cannot safely be inferred from equality-based configuration matching.

options.title: Require brokered commands and explicit sharing grants
options.body: Allow only host-brokered or allowlisted stdio commands, and require an explicit host grant before a Claw may reuse an existing global MCP declaration.

options.title: Use isolated per-Claw MCP resources
options.body: Keep Claw declarations out of the shared global name space so reuse and removal cannot affect sibling Claws.

options.title: Accept global equality-based sharing
options.body: Retain the current behavior and explicitly document that matching declarations become shared host resources with its associated execution and lifecycle risk.

recommendation.title: Require brokered commands and explicit sharing grants
recommendation.body: Allow only host-brokered or allowlisted stdio commands, and require an explicit host grant before a Claw may reuse an existing global MCP declaration.
